_comment: CRuby -> mruby API map for convert_mrbgem.rb. kind: call (rename; inject mrb as first arg when inject_mrb), macro (rename or identity, no mrb), expr (identifier replaced by an expression), type (identifier replaced), special (handled by converter code), refuse (no equivalent; marker left in output). needs_mrb marks identifiers that require an mrb_state in scope. Any CRuby-looking identifier missing from this file is refused by the converter.

type_check_refused._comment: Check_Type and rb_check_type (handler check_type in convert_mrbgem.rb) map a T_ name only when its entry has type_check exact or caveat. These names are refused with the reason given here.
type_check_refused.T_OBJECT: mruby's MRB_TT_OBJECT does not match CRuby's T_OBJECT: CRuby allocates exceptions as T_OBJECT (ruby4src error.c:3583 via object.c:118), mruby allocates them as MRB_TT_EXCEPTION (src/error.c:42), so the check would reject exceptions
type_check_refused.T_CLASS: mruby's MRB_TT_CLASS does not match CRuby's T_CLASS: a CRuby singleton class is a class with RUBY_FL_SINGLETON (ruby4src class.c:42), mruby allocates singleton classes as MRB_TT_SCLASS (src/class.c:371), so the check would reject them
type_check_refused.RUBY_T_NIL: nil and false share mruby's tag MRB_TT_FALSE (include/mruby/value.h:106, MRB_TT_FALSE; mrb_nil_p tells them apart by value, value.h:184), so a type check cannot tell nil from false
type_check_refused.T_NIL: nil and false share mruby's tag MRB_TT_FALSE (include/mruby/value.h:106, MRB_TT_FALSE; mrb_nil_p tells them apart by value, value.h:184), so a type check cannot tell nil from false
type_check_refused.T_FALSE: mruby's MRB_TT_FALSE (include/mruby/value.h:106) also matches nil, which CRuby reports as T_NIL
type_check_refused.T_TRUE: not in the type-check subset of this change (refused as listed); mruby's MRB_TT_TRUE (include/mruby/value.h:107) is true only, so it can be added as its own change
type_check_refused.T_UNDEF: CRuby's Qundef is an internal marker, not a Ruby object type; mruby's MRB_TT_UNDEF (value.h:111) is a separate value kind
type_check_refused.T_STRUCT: the fork has no MRB_TT_STRUCT tag (include/mruby/value.h:106-131); Struct instances are an mrbgem class (mrbgems/mruby-struct), so a type test would be a class test, which is not made here
type_check_refused.T_REGEXP: stuck point (Regexp): a T_REGEXP tag has no mruby tag to compare with (include/mruby/value.h:106-131): a Regexp is the mruby-onig-regexp data object, so the test is its data type, which RB_TYPE_P and a switch on TYPE use (the switch pass); this bare use has no such test

unmapped_reasons.T_RATIONAL: stuck point (gem dependency): a Rational test is the mruby-rational class test, which needs the state and the gem (the decision is made: the gem is a dependency when the test is emitted); a bare use has no test to make here
unmapped_reasons.T_COMPLEX: stuck point (gem dependency): a Complex test is the mruby-complex class test, which needs the state and the gem (the decision is made: the gem is a dependency when the test is emitted); a bare use has no test to make here
unmapped_reasons._comment: A name with no api_map entry is refused with the reason given here (the converter's no-entry path). PRIsVALUE is converted where rb_raise and rb_sprintf take it; elsewhere it is an argument of rb_enc_sprintf, which takes an rb_encoding *.
unmapped_reasons.PRIsVALUE: stuck point (PRIsVALUE): PRIsVALUE outside the format of rb_raise, rb_sprintf and rb_enc_sprintf (a VALUE argument of another call) is not converted; it has no mruby form in this position

ruby/st.h.caveat: CRuby's st.h declares the st table API and the st_retval enum; mruby has no st table (its hash is mrb_hash). The include is dropped: st_retval's ST_* return codes are mapped (ST_CONTINUE, ST_STOP as expressions), and any st_table or st_* call has no entry and is refused where it is used

rb_str_encode.caveat: CRuby's rb_str_encode(str, to, ecflags, ecopts) is mruby-encoding's rb_str_encode (the fork): the three encodings are ASCII-compatible, so a conversion among them is defined for ASCII only; an ASCII-only string takes the target tag, and other bytes raise ArgumentError (CRuby raises Encoding::UndefinedConversionError). ecflags and ecopts are not used

RB_OBJ_FROZEN_RAW.caveat: CRuby's RB_OBJ_FROZEN_RAW tests the frozen bit of an object's flags; the fork keeps it in the object's basic header (MRB_FL_OBJ_IS_FROZEN, include/mruby/object.h), tested for heap objects only (an immediate has no flags, so it is not frozen here)

rb_marshal_load.caveat: CRuby's rb_marshal_load(port) reads a marshalled object from a string: the mruby-marshal gem (3rd/mruby-marshal) provides mrb_marshal_load(mrb, str), and the converted gem depends on it (api_map gem_dep). The argument is a String, as CRuby's port reads from one

rb_reg_new.caveat: CRuby's rb_reg_new(src, len, options) is a Regexp: the mruby-onig-regexp gem (3rd/mruby-onig-regexp, Onigmo) provides OnigRegexp, built with the same options, and the converted code builds an OnigRegexp (OnigRegexp.new(source, options)). The class is OnigRegexp, not Regexp; the options are passed as given (CRuby ONIG_OPTION_* values, e.g. IGNORECASE)

rb_time_timespec_new.caveat: CRuby's rb_time_timespec_new(ts, offset): offset INT_MAX is local time, INT_MAX-1 is UTC, and any other is a fixed UTC offset in seconds (mrb_time_at_offset, mruby-time in the fork). mruby's Time keeps microseconds, so the nanoseconds are divided by 1000

T_NONE.caveat: CRuby's T_NONE is the no-type tag (a sentinel, e.g. oj's fast.c parent_type = T_NONE for no parent); the fork has no empty-object tag, so the sentinel is MRB_TT_UNDEF (include/mruby/value.h:113), which no Ruby object carries

RB_ENC_INTERNED_STR_NULL_CHECK.caveat: a CRuby build flag, not a runtime value: msgpack's extconf.rb defines it as 1 only for Ruby 3.0.0 to 3.0.5 (the CRuby bug ruby/ruby#18772, where an interned empty string had a null encoding), and buffer.h defaults it to 0. The mruby port has no such Ruby version and no interned-string null encoding, so the check is the default 0 (its branch is dead)

RUBY_T_NONE.caveat: CRuby's RUBY_T_NONE is the no-type tag: the sentinel MRB_TT_UNDEF (include/mruby/value.h:113), as for T_NONE

rb_thread_local_aref.caveat: CRuby's thread-local storage (rb_thread_local_aref/aset of a symbol key): a per-state hash in a global of the mrb_state. Each mruby-uv thread has its own mrb_state, so each thread has its own values; the thread argument is ignored, and a state shared between threads shares its values

rb_str_cat2.caveat: appends the NUL-terminated bytes; returns the string, as CRuby

rb_str_cat_cstr.caveat: appends the NUL-terminated bytes; returns the string, as CRuby

rb_define_alloc_func.caveat: the allocator becomes the class's allocate and new (singleton methods, see the prelude); a subclass uses its superclass's allocator

rb_thread_current.caveat: the fork has no Thread: the current thread is nil (a single-threaded runtime; thread-local storage stays a stuck point)

rb_mutex_new.caveat: the fork has no Mutex: a mutex is nil; lock and unlock do nothing (a single-threaded runtime never contends for a lock)

rb_mutex_lock.caveat: no-op: a single-threaded runtime never contends for a lock

rb_mutex_unlock.caveat: no-op: a single-threaded runtime never contends for a lock

rb_undef_alloc_func.caveat: mruby has no separate allocator: the class's new is undefined, so Klass.new raises NoMethodError where CRuby raises TypeError (allocator undefined); the argument must be a tracked class variable

RB_OBJ_WRITTEN.caveat: the object must be a heap value; the old value is not needed by mruby's field barrier, as CRuby's write barrier does not need it

SSIZET2NUM.caveat: CRuby's Integer from a C size (signed for SSIZET2NUM): mruby's fixnum; a value beyond mruby's integer range is not represented

SIZET2NUM.caveat: CRuby's Integer from a C size (signed for SSIZET2NUM): mruby's fixnum; a value beyond mruby's integer range is not represented

rb_const_set.caveat: the class is a VALUE here (mrb_const_set takes an mrb_value); the ID is an mrb_sym

rb_class_name.caveat: returns the class name as a String (CRuby returns a VALUE); the argument is a class value

rb_id2sym.caveat: an ID is an mrb_sym here; the Symbol value is mrb_symbol_value

rb_intern2.caveat: interns the bytes (length given), as CRuby's rb_intern2

rb_mEnumerable.caveat: Enumerable is a mruby gem module (mruby-enumerator); looked up by name, raises at run time if the gem is not loaded

rb_mComparable.caveat: Comparable is looked up by name, as Enumerable

rb_str_concat.caveat: appends the other value to the string and returns the string, as CRuby's rb_str_concat

RB_OBJ_FREEZE.caveat: freezes the object; the result is not used (CRuby's RB_OBJ_FREEZE is void)

LL2NUM.caveat: an mruby fixnum; a value beyond mruby's integer range is not represented

NUM2SSIZET.caveat: converts through mruby's integer conversion (see NUM2INT)

NUM2USHORT.caveat: converts through mruby's integer conversion (see NUM2INT)

NUM2ULL.caveat: converts through mruby's integer conversion (see NUM2INT)

rb_bug.caveat: the format is printed by mruby's formatter; CRuby's PRIsVALUE arguments are not mapped (refused where they appear)

rb_fatal.caveat: mrb_bug (src/error.c) prints the message and exits, as CRuby's rb_fatal does: it is not an exception, so no rescue sees it. The prefix differs (CRuby prints [FATAL], mruby prints bug:); CRuby's PRIsVALUE arguments are not mapped

rb_sprintf.caveat: returns a String built by mruby's formatter (see rb_bug for the format); PRIsVALUE in the format becomes %S (%!S for the + flag)

rb_ary_new_from_values.caveat: copies the n values into a new Array, as CRuby's rb_ary_new_from_values

FIXNUM_MAX.caveat: CRuby's FIXNUM_MAX (2^62-1 on 64-bit): the value is kept, so the converted code makes the same Fixnum/Bignum decisions; the mruby integer is wider, so a value in this range is still an mruby fixnum

FIXNUM_MIN.caveat: CRuby's FIXNUM_MIN (-2^62 on 64-bit): the value is kept (see FIXNUM_MAX)

rb_rational_new2.caveat: needs the mruby-rational gem (its Kernel#Rational and Rational#numerator / denominator); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build

rb_rational_new.caveat: needs the mruby-rational gem (its Kernel#Rational and Rational#numerator / denominator); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build

rb_struct_aref.caveat: needs the mruby-struct gem (Struct#[] and Struct#size); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build

RSTRUCT_GET.caveat: needs the mruby-struct gem (Struct#[]); the index is a C integer here (CRuby's RSTRUCT_GET takes a long), so it is converted to an Integer value

RSTRUCT_LEN.caveat: needs the mruby-struct gem (Struct#[] and Struct#size); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build; the length is an mrb_int (as CRuby's long)

rb_time_nano_new.caveat: needs the mruby-time gem (Time.at); mruby's Time keeps microseconds, so the nanoseconds are divided by 1000 (the sub-microsecond part is dropped)

rb_time_new.caveat: needs the mruby-time gem (Time.at with seconds and microseconds, as CRuby's rb_time_new)

rb_enc_interned_str.caveat: the encoding argument is dropped (mruby strings carry no encoding): the bytes are kept; CRuby's interned string is frozen, this one is not

rb_enc_str_asciicompat_p.caveat: mruby strings are byte strings with no encoding, so every string is taken as ASCII-compatible; a CRuby string in a non-ASCII-compatible encoding (UTF-16) has no mruby form

rb_obj_method_arity.caveat: needs the mruby-method gem (Object#method and Method#arity); the call raises at run time if the gem is not in the build; the arity is a C int (CRuby's rb_obj_method_arity returns int)

rb_big2str.caveat: calls to_s with the base (Integer#to_s), as CRuby's rb_big2str

rb_cstr2inum.caveat: parses the C string in the base without the badcheck (CRuby's rb_cstr2inum with badcheck off)

ST2FIX.caveat: a st_data_t / st_index_t value is a fixnum here (as INT2FIX); the value must fit mruby's integer

rb_io_write.caveat: calls write on the IO (mruby-io), as CRuby's rb_io_write

rb_enc_copy.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding, so copying one's encoding to another does nothing

rb_must_asciicompat.caveat: every mruby string is ASCII-compatible (see rb_enc_str_asciicompat_p), so the check always passes

rb_ary_new3.caveat: a literal count; the values are an mrb_value array (mrb_ary_new_from_values)

rb_to_int.caveat: converts the value to an Integer (to_int), as CRuby's rb_to_int

rb_exc_new2.caveat: a new exception of the class with the message (CRuby's rb_exc_new2); the class must be a tracked class variable

rb_yield_values2.caveat: yields the argc values of argv to the block (as rb_yield_values2); valid only in a registered method (the block is fetched by its wrapper)

rb_check_typeddata.caveat: checks the value's data type and returns its pointer (mruby's mrb_data_get_ptr raises on another type), as CRuby's rb_check_typeddata

rb_obj_call_init.caveat: calls initialize on the object with argc values from argv (CRuby's rb_obj_call_init)

rb_int_positive_pow.caveat: x ** y on Integers (Integer#**), as CRuby's rb_int_positive_pow

rb_struct_s_members.caveat: the struct class's members (mruby-struct's Struct.members), as CRuby's rb_struct_s_members; needs the struct gem

RB_ALLOC.caveat: allocates the bytes with mrb_malloc (raises on failure, as CRuby's xmalloc raises NoMemoryError); the pointer is void * as in CRuby

RB_ALLOC_N.caveat: n values of the type, allocated with mrb_malloc (see RB_ALLOC)

RB_REALLOC_N.caveat: reallocates the variable to n values of the type with mrb_realloc (see RB_ALLOC_N)

rb_gc.caveat: a full collection, as CRuby's rb_gc

rb_hash.caveat: calls hash on the object (Object#hash), as CRuby's rb_hash

rb_singleton_class.caveat: the singleton class of the value, as CRuby's rb_singleton_class (returns a VALUE in both)

rb_alias.caveat: aliases the method of the class (the class must be a tracked class variable; the names are IDs, mrb_sym here)

rb_str_to_inum.caveat: parses the string in the base; badcheck as given (CRuby's rb_str_to_inum)

rb_num_coerce_cmp.caveat: CRuby's rb_num_coerce_cmp: y.coerce(x) gives [a, b], and a.op(b) is the result; nil when y does not coerce (no rescue: a coerce that raises propagates)

rb_num_coerce_bin.caveat: CRuby's rb_num_coerce_bin: y.coerce(x) gives [a, b], and a.op(b) is the result (a TypeError from coerce propagates)

rb_num_coerce_relop.caveat: CRuby's rb_num_coerce_relop: the coerced comparison; when it cannot be made, it raises ArgumentError (comparison failed), as CRuby's rb_cmperr

rb_opts_exception_p.caveat: CRuby's rb_opts_exception_p: the :exception option of an options hash (nil or no key: the default); true/false; anything else raises ArgumentError (as CRuby)

rb_typeddata_is_kind_of.caveat: CRuby's rb_typeddata_is_kind_of(obj, &type): obj is a typed data object whose type is type (or a subclass of it in CRuby). mruby's data objects carry one type descriptor and no parent chain, so this is an exact match; the second argument is the address of the type, as in the bigdecimal use

PRIuSIZE.caveat: C99 printf length modifier for size_t (CRuby's PRIuSIZE is this string literal)

rb_memsearch.caveat: CRuby's rb_memsearch(x, m, y, n, enc) is the byte offset of the m-byte x in the n-byte y, or -1; the encoding is dropped (mruby strings carry none), so the search is bytewise

RB_ALLOCV_N.caveat: CRuby's RB_ALLOCV_N(type, v, n) allocates a temporary buffer freed by RB_ALLOCV_END(v); converted to mrb_malloc, with the free at RB_ALLOCV_END of the same pointer (the declaration and the end must be in one function, with no return or goto between)

RB_ALLOCV_END.caveat: the free of the buffer RB_ALLOCV_N allocated for this VALUE: mrb_free of that pointer

ALLOCV_N.caveat: the unprefixed form of RB_ALLOCV_N (CRuby's ruby/util.h alias): the same temporary buffer, converted the same way

ALLOCV_END.caveat: the unprefixed form of RB_ALLOCV_END: the same free

PRIdVALUE.caveat: C99 printf length modifier for a signed VALUE (CRuby's PRIdVALUE is PRI_VALUE_PREFIX "l" followed by d, which is "ld" on LP64)

MEMMOVE.caveat: CRuby's MEMMOVE(p, src, type, n) is memmove(p, src, sizeof(type)*n); the type is a plain name here (VALUE is the fork's mrb_value)

MEMCPY.caveat: CRuby's MEMCPY(p, src, type, n) is memcpy(p, src, sizeof(type)*n) (the type is a plain name here)

ALLOCA_N.caveat: CRuby's ALLOCA_N(type, n) is the C alloca of n elements of type; the fork's build uses the C library's alloca, so the call is the same

PRIdSIZE.caveat: C99 printf length modifier for size_t (CRuby's PRIdSIZE is this string literal)

DECIMAL_SIZE_OF_BITS.caveat: CRuby's DECIMAL_SIZE_OF_BITS(n) is the number of decimal digits that n bits can need: (n * 146 / 485) + 1 (CRuby's util headers; pure arithmetic)

rb_enc_interned_str_cstr.caveat: CRuby's rb_enc_interned_str_cstr(cstr, enc) is an interned string in the encoding enc; mruby strings carry no encoding (the default is UTF-8 here), so the encoding argument is ignored and the string is a plain mruby string

RUBY_API_VERSION_CODE.caveat: the CRuby API version the gem emulates: 2.2 (20200), by the user's decision (fast_blank: CRuby 2.2 or later, so U+180E is not whitespace). The build also defines it (--define RUBY_API_VERSION_CODE=20200), which selects the #ifndef branches

STRNCASECMP.caveat: CRuby's STRNCASECMP (ruby/util.h) is the C library's strncasecmp (its name, as a macro value)

STRTOUL.caveat: CRuby's STRTOUL (ruby/util.h) is the C library's strtoul

PRI_SIZE_PREFIX.caveat: CRuby's PRI_SIZE_PREFIX is the printf length modifier for size_t, the string the PRI*SIZE macros append to (C99 z)

PUREFUNC.caveat: PUREFUNC (CRuby's pure-function attribute) is a compiler hint: the declaration it wraps is kept, without the attribute

RARRAY_PTR.caveat: mruby's RARRAY_PTR (include/mruby/array.h) is the array's element pointer, as CRuby's; the use reads elements. A write through it would need mruby's array modify step (not done here)

rb_long2int.caveat: CRuby's rb_long2int: the long as an int, raising RangeError when it does not fit (a checked conversion, as CRuby's)

rb_check_symbol_cstr.caveat: CRuby's rb_check_symbol_cstr: the symbol of the name when one exists, nil otherwise (callers test for nil, as oj does); the encoding argument is dropped (mruby symbols carry no encoding)

rb_get_kwargs.caveat: CRuby's rb_get_kwargs: the values of the listed keywords (Qundef when an optional one is absent); a missing required keyword raises ArgumentError. Unknown keywords are not rejected (a caveat: CRuby rejects them unless the method takes **rest)

rb_str_dump.caveat: CRuby's rb_str_dump: the String#dump of the string (mruby-string-ext's String#dump, a fork gem). Its escapes follow mruby's, which may differ from CRuby's for non-ASCII bytes

rb_cstr_to_dbl.caveat: parses the NUL-terminated string as a Float; badcheck as given (CRuby's rb_cstr_to_dbl), raising ArgumentError on a bad string

rb_check_convert_type.caveat: returns nil when the value has no conversion method, as CRuby; the type is the mruby MRB_TT_ tag (T_STRING and the other T_ tags map to it)

rb_need_block.caveat: raises LocalJumpError when the method has no block, as CRuby's rb_need_block; it reads the block of the enclosing method, so it is supported only where the mruby state is in scope

RB_FLOAT_TYPE_P.caveat: a Float test (mruby's float tag), as CRuby's RB_FLOAT_TYPE_P

rb_special_const_p.caveat: an immediate value (no heap object), as CRuby's special constant test (the immediates differ: mruby's are not CRuby's)

RSTRING_GETMEM.caveat: the pointer and length of the string, as CRuby's RSTRING_GETMEM
